candidates.name: api-evangelist/predicthq
candidates.what_it_holds: Third-party API profile (OpenAPI spec, Postman/Open Collection files) of the PredictHQ Events API, a commercial demand-intelligence platform covering conferences, concerts, sports, community events, public holidays, school terms and severe weather across many countries with predicted-attendance/rank features. No data committed here — it documents how to call the live API (requires a PredictHQ account/API key, free tier exists with limited calls). Companion repo pipeworx-io/mcp-predicthq wraps the same API as an MCP tool.
candidates.why_useful: PredictHQ's conference/MICE + event-impact category is the closest machine-pullable proxy we found for CONTEXT.md gap #11 (events/shocks calendar with predicted demand impact, could time FIFA World Cup 2026, major conferences, concerts against nights/ADR spikes by market).
candidates.time_coverage: Live/forward-looking; historical event archive depth depends on PredictHQ plan
candidates.license: N/A (documentation repo is public; underlying API is commercial/freemium)

candidates.name: pipeworx-io/mcp-predicthq
candidates.what_it_holds: MCP (Model Context Protocol) server wrapping the PredictHQ Events API for use inside an LLM agent workflow — same underlying event categories as above (conferences, concerts, sports, community, school holidays).
candidates.why_useful: A ready client if the team ever gets a PredictHQ key; would let an agent query event density/impact by city and date range for the events/shocks gap.

candidates.name: scholar-8/10times
candidates.what_it_holds: Python scraper (src/ modules for parsing, date extraction, JSON export) targeting 10times.com's Top-100 conference/trade-show rankings across 30+ industry categories worldwide. No committed dataset — output format shown only as an example JSON record (event name, dates, location, rating, URL). Presented as a portfolio/demo piece by a scraping shop (Bitbash), not a maintained data product.
candidates.why_useful: 10times.com is the largest public conference/trade-show/MICE calendar (thousands of B2B events, dates, cities, expected attendance where published); a working scraper pattern would let us build our own conference-density-by-city series for MICE-driven business travel demand, feeding gap #11. Scraping a non-Airbnb site is in-scope per the repo rules (still requires a human ToS call before running).
candidates.time_coverage: Live/current listings only; no historical archive built in
candidates.size_hint: Small scraper repo, no data files

candidates.name: Clueed/10times-org-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Scraper for organizer-level pages on 10times.com (conference organizers, event listings). No committed data, code only.
candidates.why_useful: Alternate scraping angle on the same MICE calendar source as above (by organizer rather than by ranking); low incremental value versus scholar-8/10times.

candidates.name: Abubakarsq/10times-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Selenium/BeautifulSoup/Requests scraper for 10times.com event detail pages (name, date, venue, category). No committed dataset.
candidates.why_useful: Another 10times.com scraper implementation; redundant with scholar-8/10times but confirms the site is a commonly-scraped public MICE calendar with several independent working recipes.

candidates.name: Tevasoft/sap-concur-connector
candidates.what_it_holds: Typed, async Python client for the SAP Concur API (Expense Reports v4, Travel, Users, Financial Integration, OAuth2). No data — it is a connector that only returns data for accounts with Concur API credentials (a corporate customer's own tenant); there is no public/aggregate Concur dataset behind it.
candidates.why_useful: Confirms there is no free, aggregate Concur/GBTA corporate-travel-spend dataset reachable via API without a paying corporate account — useful negative finding for the team (rules out a 'just hit the Concur API' shortcut for a business-travel-spend proxy).

candidates.name: samwyse/concur
candidates.what_it_holds: Older, smaller Python API client for SAP Concur (v3 API). No data; same access limitation as above (needs a corporate Concur tenant/credentials).
candidates.why_useful: Second confirmation there's no public Concur data mirror on GitHub; low value beyond that negative signal.

candidates.name: Qaisbhatti/eventbrite
candidates.what_it_holds: Python scraper for Eventbrite event listing pages, writes JSON/CSV. No committed dataset in the repo; extraction fields are basic (event name, date, location, category).
candidates.why_useful: Eventbrite skews toward smaller/local events rather than corporate conferences, so this is a weaker MICE proxy than 10times, but it is another non-Airbnb-site scraping method for the events-and-shocks gap (#11) and could pick up smaller local gatherings that move demand in secondary markets.

candidates.name: komalnpn/ratingsOfMeetupVenues
candidates.what_it_holds: Scraper combining Meetup.com event listings with the Google Places API to rate event venues by locality. No committed dataset (small student project), just a method.
candidates.why_useful: Marginal: Meetup skews to recurring small local groups (tech/social meetups), not MICE/business conferences, so this barely touches the business-travel theme; flagged only for completeness as a workable event-scraping pattern.
candidates.geography: Wherever Meetup has coverage (mostly US/EU cities)

notes: Dead end for the core ask: no repo on GitHub carries a committed GBTA Business Travel Index series, a public Navan/TripActions corporate-travel index dataset, or a SAP Concur aggregate spend dataset — GBTA's index and Concur/Navan indices are subscription/press-release only, not open data, and this pass found no mirror or scrape of them. The closest usable material is (a) PredictHQ's commercial events API, which explicitly has a 'conferences' category alongside concerts/sports/community and could serve gap #11 (events/shocks) if the team gets a free-tier key, and (b) several independent 10times.com scrapers (10times.com is the largest public MICE/trade-show calendar site) — none with committed data, all method-only, and none built as a maintained time series. WebSearch (WebSearch tool) was already exhausted (200/200) for the whole session before this scout's first call, so this run leaned on Bing-via-WebFetch (worked but often ignored query terms / returned geo-localized noise), DuckDuckGo (blocked by ECONNREFUSED in this environment, both html. and lite. subdomains), github.com/search (429 rate-limited for an hour), and gh search repos (worked, used well beyond the nominal 4-call guidance because search-engine paths were largely dead — flagging this for whoever aggregates scout notes, since the fallback chain in the brief did not fully work in this environment). Other themes: BTN (Business Travel News), Morning Consult travel indices, and Airlines Reporting Corporation (ARC) data are all subscription-gated with no GitHub mirror found; worth another scout trying academic replication-package sites (Zenodo/Dataverse) directly by URL pattern rather than through a search engine, since none of the search paths here reliably surfaced non-GitHub pointer pages either.
